description: Conversion of upper floors from residential unit (Class C3) to (HMO) house in multiple occupancy (Class C4), involving part single, part 2-storey side extension to also facilitate enlargement of ground floor commercial unit (Class E) with extension to roof at side, habitable room in loft with rear dormer, front and side rooflights, additional windows and door at side elevation and associated cycle and refuse storage.
decision_conditions: The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the end of three years from the date of this permission. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans:002.26/01002.26/02002.26/05002.26/07002.26/00002.26/03002.26/08002.26/06002.26/04Planning StatementReason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

All new external work shall be carried out in materials that resemble, as closely as possible, in colour and texture as specified in the approved application.Reason: To safeguard the appearance of the premises and the character of the immediate area.

The glazing serving the additional side windows at first floor, as seen along the proposed side elevation of the development indicated on drawing No. 002.26/08, shall be in obscured glass with an equivalent obscuration as level 3 on the Pilkington Obscuration Range and the window shall be non-opening unless the parts of the window which can be opened are more than 1.7 metres above the floor of the room in which the window is installed. The glazing shall not be altered without the approval in writing of the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To safeguard the privacy of the occupiers of adjoining and neighbouring properties

The use of the property as a House in Multiple Occupation hereby approved shall be occupied by a maximum of 4 people at any one time acting as a single household and shall not be subdivided or occupied as self-contained units. Reason: To accord with the stipulations of definition as a House of Multiple Occupation and to safeguard the residential character of the surrounding area.

No independent cooking or laundry facilities shall be installed in any of the respective bedrooms and the communal kitchen / dining rooms shall be retained in perpetuity.Reason: To accord with the stipulations of definition as a House of Multiple Occupation and to safeguard the amenity of neighbours and the residential character of the surrounding area

The development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until the four-cycle parking spaces have been fully constructed in accordance with the hereby approved details and shall thereafter be retained for the lifetime of the development. Reason: To ensure that adequate cycle parking facilities are provided to promote sustainable modes of transport.

The development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until waste storage and recycling facilities to satisfy the future number of occupiers on site have been provided within the development, in accordance with the Enfield's Household Recycling and Waste Planning Guidance for New Developments (February 2024). Such facilities to be retained for the lifetime of the development.Reason: To ensure that adequate waste and recycling storage facilities are provided to meet the needs of future occupiers, promote sustainable waste management practices, and support borough-wide recycling targets.

The development shall not commence until a Sustainable Drainage Strategy has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall be based on the disposal of surface water by means of a sustainable drainage system in accordance with the principles as set out in the Technical Guidance to the National Planning Policy Framework and should be in line with our DMD Policy SuDS Requirements: Shall be designed to a 1 in 1 and 1 in 100 year storm event with the allowance for climate changeFollow the London Plan Drainage Hierarchy and providing evidence of the potential for full infiltration SuDS and maximising above ground storage Follow the SuDS management train by providing source control for the site, and a number of treatment phases corresponding to their pollution potential Maximise opportunities for sustainable development, improve water quality, biodiversity, local amenity and recreation value The system must be designed to allow for flows that exceed the design capacity to be stored on site or conveyed off-site with minimum impact Clear ownership, management and maintenance arrangements must be established The details submitted shall include levels, sizing, cross sections and specifications for all drainage featuresREASON: To ensure the sustainable management of water, minimise flood risk, minimise discharge of surface water outside of the curtilage of the property and ensure that the drainage system will remain functional throughout the lifetime of the development in accordance with Policy CP28 of the Core Strategy, DMD Policy 61, and Policies SI12 & SI13 of the London Plan and the NPPF and to maximise opportunities for sustainable development, improve water quality, biodiversity, local amenity and recreation value.

Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved (including demolition and all preparatory work), a full specification and design for the foundations shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The specification shall demonstrate adherence to the guidelines set out in NHBC Chapter 4.2 Building near Trees. Reason: Required prior to commencement of development to satisfy the Local Planning Authority that the development will be adequately constructed against a risk of future subsidence and to ensure that the current street tree, or any future street tree, will not be at risk through implication in possible future subsidence cases, in accordance with Policy DMD80(b) (Trees on Development Sites) and pursuant to section 197 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

The completed schedule of site supervision and monitoring of the arboricultural protection measures as approved in condition (11) shall be submitted for approval in writing by the Local Planning Authority within 28 days from completion of the development hereby permitted. This condition may only be fully discharged on completion of the development, subject to satisfactory written evidence of compliance through contemporaneous supervision and monitoring of the tree protection throughout construction by a suitably qualified and pre-appointed tree specialist.Reason: In order to ensure compliance with the tree protection and arboricultural supervision details submitted under condition 11 pursuant to section 197 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 in accordance with Policy DMD80

Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved (including demolition and all preparatory work), a scheme for the protection of the street tree compliant with BS 5837:2012 shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme will comprise a detailed Arboricultural Method Statement (AMS) report supplemented by Tree Protection Plan(s) (TPP). The plan(s) shall be of legible scale and clearly show the layout (as agreed), all relevant existing site features that form a consideration within the protection scheme, and the location/extent of all appropriate protection measures. Specific matters to be addressed within the AMS and TPPs will include:a)location and installation of all utility services/drainage, avoiding the Root Protection Areas (RPA) of the tree (RPA as defined within BS 5837:2012);b)methods of removal of existing hard standing and kerb edging within or directly adjacent to RPAs;c)method of installation of the foundations (foundations as specified in the details submitted to discharge the foundations condition);d)a full specification for the construction of all paths, parking areas and driveways (including alterations to the existing layout of hard standing) within RPAs. Where a no-dig sub-base is specified (e.g. cellular confinement system) a specification shall be provided (including a diagrammatical cross-section of the product in-situ) and extent of areas where this would be implemented illustrated within the TPP;e)detailed levels and cross-sections to show that the raised levels of surfacing where the installation of no-dig surfacing within RPAs is proposed, demonstrating that the raised areas can be effectively integrated with prevailing levels where they meet with adjacent surfacing or building damp proof courses;f)a full specification for the installation of boundary treatments within or directly adjacent to RPAs;g)a specification for tree protection to safeguard all trees during both demolition and construction phases. The Tree Protection Plan(s) shall clearly indicate the alignment of the tree protection fencing, trunk protection, and extent of ground protection;h)a specification for scaffolding and ground protection in Construction Exclusion Zones (where necessary);i)details of site access, temporary parking, on site welfare facilities, loading, unloading and storage of equipment, materials, fuels and waste as well concrete mixing and siting of fires;j) an auditable scheme of arboricultural supervision and inspection of tree protection measures by a suitably qualified arboriculturist. This will include, but not be limited to, supervision of the removal of hard surfacing, installation of foundations, boundary treatment, surface treatment.This condition shall not be discharged before details of the foundations as required by attached condition 10 have been received and approved.The development thereafter shall be implemented in strict accordance with the approved details.Reason: Required prior to commencement of development to satisfy the Local Planning Authority that the trees to be retained will not be damaged during demolition or construction and to protect and enhance the appearance and character of the site and locality, in accordance with Policy DMD80 (Trees on Development Sites) and pursuant to section 197 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.
